result:
The goal step now shows **Today** in the training start date box on a new plan, and clicking it brings up the same date picker. If you don't touch it, the plan starts today. All the tests pass on temporary copies of the project, and the real database and the login and signup templates are untouched. I also ran the flow on a temporary copy in Chrome with a script, and screenshots of both states look right.

**One thing I got wrong: your weekly checkbox was never built.** My reply to that request was just "No response requested", and I did no work on it. A search of the code confirms nothing was added. Your request is still open, so do you want me to build it next?

**How the start date behaves**

| Situation | What the box shows |
|---|---|
| New plan, untouched | "Today"; the plan starts today |
| After clicking "Today" | The date picker, set to today, with past dates rejected |
| A later date chosen, then returning to the step | That date in the picker |
| A past date submitted anyway | The picker with the existing error |
| Editing a plan whose saved start is today | "Today" |
| Editing a plan with any other start date | That date in the picker, as now |

**Things to know**
- **Choosing a date takes two clicks:** the first swaps "Today" for the date box, and the second opens the calendar. Opening the calendar on the first click would need JavaScript.
- **It can't switch back to "Today" on the same page:** once the date box is showing, it stays until the page reloads. If you pick today's date again and move on, you'll see "Today" when you return to the step.
- **Leaving the page open past midnight:** "Today" still holds the date the page loaded, so Next gives the past-date error and shows the picker.

Keyboard users can tab to the box and press Space to reveal the picker.

**Files changed:** `templates/setup.html`, `main.py` (passes today's date to the page) and `static/style.css`.
